scoringCalibration: No point is awarded yet. The eyelashes now use finer, denser, shorter curved fibers with deterministic three-fiber direction groups and explicit cornea clearance, but integrated eyelid margins and canthus topology remain below strict review quality.
visualFindings: The front view no longer shows the long, evenly spaced radial spikes of v50.
Upper lashes are shorter in screen-space because most length projects forward before curling upward.
Lower lashes are thinner and lower contrast while remaining visible in the close view.
Three-fiber direction groups break the picket-fence rhythm without producing large artificial clumps.
rejectedExperiments: Increasing only the lower-lash body clearance was rejected because one curved segment still intersected the left cornea.
Deleting or hand-special-casing the offending left lash was rejected in favor of a reusable cornea-distance projection rule.
blockingFailures: Integrated upper and lower eyelid thickness and expression-compatible canthus topology remain below review quality.
The face still needs stronger anatomical plane transitions and less procedural commissure geometry.
The crown needs a coherent authored direction field with a narrower irregular part and fewer cross-flow fibers.
Hair shading still needs an engine-side dual-lobe anisotropic model and strand-scale roughness variation.
Clothing edge flow, seams, folds, materials and outer layers remain below review quality.
Raised-arm shoulders still require corrective deformation and the standard pose suite remains incomplete.
Signed clothing-distance samples remain negative despite zero exact triangle overlaps in the audited frames.
LOD transition popping and frame-time impact remain untested in the website renderer.
